label: copy-phase re-input of k/o/u late in long sequences (context-gated)
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (~0.03% of steps), active only in the copy phase, never in the original or delimiter phases. Nearly all activations are on steps where the fed-back input is k (about 67% of mass), o (22%) or u (8%), at recall_idx >= 3, mostly in L=8-9 sequences (95% of mass). The largest activations are on k (or o) a few steps into the copy, usually right after v, m or h has been input (e.g. ...m v h [o]..., ...v [k]...). Requiring that v/m/h appeared earlier keeps about 85% of the mass, but precision stays around 3%: the unit fires on only a small, context-dependent fraction of k/o/u copy steps, and I could not find a simple prefix condition that explains which ones. It does not fire on other tokens apart from rare p/r/a/t, on original-phase steps, or on short sequences (L<=6).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=k (+5.83), phase=2 & in_tok=o (+4.53), prev_tok=v (+3.33), phase=2 & out_tok=h (+2.81), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+2.73), phase=2 & out_tok=3 (+2.35). Lower it: prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.47), orig6=- (-1.86), orig7=- (-1.72), prev_tok=<DEL> (-1.65).
